endorsements.quote: Third, researchers and developers should collaborate to embed therapeutically informed design safeguards into LLMs and chatbots.

Finally, at the policy level, regulators and research bodies should develop incident reporting systems for AI-related mental health events, mirroring pharmacovigilance models, and require algorithmic transparency for systems marketed as supportive or therapeutic.

Psychotherapeutic interventions could include psychoeducation on digital reality testing, helping patients to identify when online or AI-mediated interactions begin to shape beliefs in maladaptive ways.

unlisted_practices: Clinicians should incorporate screening questions about AI use into routine psychiatric assessments, particularly for youth or individuals with known psychosis vulnerability.
Developers of mental health chatbots should embed CBTp-consistent guardrails that normalize uncertainty, encourage reflective distance, and redirect users toward real-world social contact.
Developers should train general-use LLMs to recognize and gently de-escalate delusional or self-referential themes rather than engage with them.
Developers should build digital red-flag algorithms that detect excessive anthropomorphism, self-referential speech, or escalating conviction while preserving user autonomy.
Clinical training programs should include modules on AI literacy and psychosis for psychiatrists, psychologists, and nurses.
Researchers should conduct prospective longitudinal studies measuring dose-response relationships between AI exposure, stress physiology, and psychotic symptoms.
Health agencies and research councils should promote open-source safety auditing and transparent documentation of adverse psychological outcomes from AI.
Stakeholders should establish data-sharing agreements enabling cross-disciplinary research on AI mental health harms while protecting user privacy.
Public health bodies should develop environmental cognitive remediation, family and community education, and media literacy programs to reduce AI-related cognitive distortions.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint/conceptual framework paper reviewing 'AI psychosis' and recommending research agendas, governance frameworks, and therapeutic design safeguards for AI chatbots.
